summary: Order submit failures (~31% error rate, 504s) are caused by the EXTERNAL exchange partner degrading, not by order-service v2.15.2. Onset is 11:01:25 (first "upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example" in exchange-gateway), ~13 min AFTER the 10:48 deploy. exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms jumped 120ms→~9250ms and upstream_error_rate 0.3%→~46%; it returned 503s from exchange-api and its circuit breaker opened at 11:03:26. order-service's errors are all "exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)". order-service and exchange-gateway show no CPU/memory/restart/pool anomalies (CPU flat 40%/30%, db_pool flat 14, 0 restarts), ruling out resource/capacity causes. Critically, the v2.15.2 rollback at 11:16 did NOT restore the error rate (still ~31% at 12:59, 1h43m post-rollback), ruling out the deployment as root cause. Category: dependency_failure, originating at the external exchange-api.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner (exchange-api) outage degrades order submits
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange provider api.exchange-partner.example / exchange-api began timing out and returning 503 at ~11:01. exchange-gateway's calls to it hit the 5s connect timeout, returning 504s to order-service's placeOrder path, which surfaced as ~31% order submit failures. The fault ORIGINATES outside our services at the third-party exchange API.

causal_chain.claim: External exchange-api degrades: connect timeouts + 503 at ~11:01
exchange-gateway circuit breaker opens for exchange-api at 11:03:26
order-service placeOrder gets 504 Gateway Timeout from exchange-gateway
order-service error rate jumps to ~31% and stays there

assumptions: exchange-api has no telemetry of its own (has_telemetry:false), so partner-side degradation is inferred from exchange-gateway's upstream metrics and error text.
No internal change to exchange-gateway or the network path to the partner occurred at 11:01.

ranked_hypotheses.title: bad_deployment: order-service v2.15.2 retry-safe submit handler overloads exchange path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Dep-5333 (10:48) added idempotency keys and a retry-safe submit handler; retries could hammer exchange-gateway and the partner, causing timeouts. REJECTED: the rollback at 11:16 did not recover the error rate (still ~31% at 12:59), exchange-gateway request_rate is flat (~271 req/s) with no load spike, and onset (11:01) is 13 min after the deploy while order-service's own CPU/pool are unremarkable.

causal_chain.claim: deploy dep-5333 -> retry storm -> partner timeouts

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rollback at 11:16 did not restore service (error rate still ~31% at 12:59); exchange-gateway request_rate stayed flat ~271 req/s; errors are explicitly upstream partner timeouts/503s, not order-service-internal failures.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource/capacity exhaustion in order-service or exchange-gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: CPU, memory, DB pool, or request load exhaustion caused the 504s. REJECTED: order-service cpu flat ~40% and db_pool_in_use flat ~14; exchange-gateway cpu flat ~30%, memory flat ~44%, 0 restarts, request_rate flat ~271 req/s.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: All resource metrics on order-service and exchange-gateway are flat and well below saturation during the incident.

facts.statement: order-service error rate rose from ~0.2% to ~31% starting the 11:02 bucket and remained elevated through 12:59.
All order-service errors are 504 Gateway Timeouts on exchange-gateway placeOrder calls.
exchange-gateway logged connect timeouts and 503s against the external host api.exchange-partner.example starting 11:01:25.
exchange-gateway upstream latency/error rates to the partner jumped to ~9250ms / ~46%, and its circuit breaker opened at 11:03:26.
order-service and exchange-gateway resource metrics (CPU, memory, DB pool, restarts, request rate) stayed flat during the incident.
The order-service v2.15.2 deploy was rolled back at 11:16, yet the error rate was still ~31% at 12:59.
pricing-engine error rate stayed flat, so the 09:20 cache TTL change had no impact.

assumptions: The external exchange-api partner is genuinely degraded rather than the network path between us and it.
No internal change to exchange-gateway or the network path to the partner occurred at 11:01.
The 504s reported by order-service are the propagated exchange-gateway 504s, not an independent order-service fault.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-2290: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (unrelated; pricing-engine error rate flat).
First exchange-gateway upstream connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example (op=placeOrder).
First 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' in exchange-gateway.
exchange-gateway circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api.
Error rate still ~31% (order-service) and ~47% (exchange-gateway) 1h43m after rollback; partner degradation ongoing.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating the rollback as the fix; the rollback is already done and did not recover service. Escalate to the exchange partner and ask for their incident status on api.exchange-partner.example.
recommended_actions.rationale: Error rate remained ~31% at 12:59, 1h43m after rollback, and the failing calls are upstream timeouts/503s from the external partner.

recommended_actions.action: Fail over to a secondary exchange route / enable partner fallback if available.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-103 resolution was exactly this ('Failed over to secondary exchange route; partner fixed').

recommended_actions.action: Confirm the exchange-gateway circuit breaker and timeouts are limiting blast radius; tune 5s connect timeout/retry budget if partner is slow-but-alive.
recommended_actions.rationale: Circuit breaker opened at 11:03:26; connect timeouts at 5000ms drive the 504s.

recommended_actions.action: Add telemetry/alerting on exchange-api (currently has_telemetry:false) so partner degradation is detected as the origin, not the symptom.
recommended_actions.rationale: The external node has no telemetry, forcing inference from exchange-gateway metrics.

data_gaps: No telemetry from the external exchange-api (has_telemetry:false), so the partner-side cause is inferred from exchange-gateway's upstream metrics and error text rather than directly observed.

market-data-service shows a rise to ~6.5% error rate at the same 11:02 bucket but produced 0 ERROR logs in the queried window; its role (if any) was not resolved and it does not appear on order-service's critical path.
order-service and exchange-gateway logs earlier than the query windows were not exhaustively checked for an earlier onset; onset is bounded by the first observed errors at ~11:01.

findings.statement: order-service error rate was ~0.2% until the 10:49 bucket, then jumped to ~31% from the 11:02 bucket and remained ~30-31% through 12:59.
The only order-service error pattern is 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' (349 matches), first at 11:02:45.

refs.quote: exchange-gateway call failed: <n> Gateway Timeout (placeOrder) orderId=<n>

findings.statement: order-service latency_p99 jumped from ~150ms to ~5300ms at the 11:02 bucket, consistent with a 5s downstream timeout.
order-service db_pool_in_use stayed flat (~14 connections) and cpu_pct stayed flat (~40%) throughout the incident, showing no resource exhaustion.

exchange-gateway errors are 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example' (163 placeOrder + 146 quoteSnapshot) and 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' (161); first at 11:01:25.

refs.quote: upstream connect timeout after <n>ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder

findings.statement: exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms jumped from ~120ms to ~9250ms and upstream_error_rate from 0.3% to ~46%, measured on the call to the external partner.
exchange-gateway circuit breaker opened for exchange-api: 'circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)' at 11:03:26.

refs.quote: circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio <n> over <n>s)

findings.statement: exchange-gateway is internally healthy: 0 restarts, cpu_pct flat ~30%, memory_pct flat ~44%, request_rate flat ~271 req/s, with INFO 'health check ok' and 'connection pool stats: healthy'.
The order-service v2.15.2 deploy (dep-5333) occurred at 10:48:00 and was rolled back at 11:16:00.
After the rollback at 11:16, order-service error rate stayed ~30-31% (11:28 30.95, 12:59 30.39) and exchange-gateway error_rate stayed ~44-47%, so the rollback did not restore service.
pricing-engine error rate stayed flat at ~0.21% throughout, so the 09:20 pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds config change did not affect it.
The dependency graph shows exchange-api is an external node (owner vendor, has_telemetry:false) reached via exchange-gateway, and order-service calls exchange-gateway over HTTP.

A prior incident HIST-103 (2025-10-21) matches: 'Order failures during exchange partner outage', services order-service+exchange-gateway, symptoms '504 on order submit', root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', category dependency_failure.
